heroHeadline: Day 674: El Chapo's Nephew 'El Chinacate' Arrested in Nogales with US Extradition Warrant; Three FGR Co-Defendants Still Missing; Standoff Day 29
heroSubtitle: 674 days of cartel civil war — May 26–28: Mexican federal forces arrested Isaí Martínez Zepeda ('El Chinacate'), El Chapo Guzmán's nephew and alleged Los Chapitos logistics operator, in Nogales, Sonora on May 26 alongside his brother Enoc ('El Vocho'). A federal court remanded El Chinacate with US extradition purposes on May 27. The same day (May 26), on-leave Governor Rubén Rocha Moya voluntarily appeared before Mexico's FGR in Culiacán — the first of the ten SDNY-indicted officials to face formal domestic questioning — alongside multiple co-defendants. FGR classified the sessions as witness testimony, not criminal charges. May 27–28: Infobae confirmed three co-defendants still have not appeared before FGR: Alberto Jorge Contreras Núñez (ex-Sinaloa investigative police chief), José Antonio Dionisio Hipólito (ex-state police deputy director), and Juan Valenzuela Milán. Extradition standoff enters Day 29: three of ten indicted officials in US custody at Brooklyn MDC (Mérida Sánchez, Díaz Vega, Inzunza Cazárez); seven including Rocha Moya and Mayor Gámez Mendívil remain in Mexico. UIF bank account freeze on Rocha Moya maintained (since May 15). El Mayo Zambada sentencing (EDNY, 3rd postponement) set July 20; Ovidio (NDIL) set July 27. La Mayiza ~90% territorial control; 13,300+ federal troops deployed under interim Governor Bonilla Valverde. Running conflict toll: ~2,425+ homicides (Noroeste) / 3,000+ (WSJ) since September 9, 2024; ~5,800 disappearances (NGO Sabuesos Unidas AC).
